 Apple services down, as Apple Pay, App Store and Apple Support experience outages 
 By 
 Ariel Zilber 
 Published 
 Nov. 17, 2026, 1:05 p.m. ET 
 See more of our coverage in your search results. 
 Make New York Post a Preferred Source 
 Apple users were hit with widespread service disruptions Tuesday afternoon, with thousands of outage reports involving Apple Pay, iCloud and Apple Support flooding the tracking site Downdetector.
 Complaints surged shortly after noon EST, with users reported being locked out of their Apple accounts, unable to activate new devices and encountering errors while attempting to access cloud services.
 Follow for live updates on the nationwide cyber outages affecting major online services 
 “Failed to verify your identity. Try again,” one user, identified as Tom Perkins, wrote on Downdetector, quoting an error message.

 “This has been going on for about 30 minutes.”

 Another user, identified as Steve, complained: “Can’t activate devices or log into Apple Business.”
 The trouble appeared to extend beyond the US, with complaints posted by users in Brazil, Greece and Latvia.
 “[N]ot working here in Latvia. Apple Pay doesn’t work as well, asking for sign-in which is not working,” one commenter wrote.
 4 
 A woman holds an iPhone to make a payment using Apple Pay. DenPhoto – stock.adobe.com 
 Advertisement
 The disruption comes amid a string of major technology failures across the country.
 On Monday, JPMorgan Chase suffered a systems outage that disrupted banking transactions, while United Airlines experienced an internal technology failure that delayed departures.
 Last week, a Microsoft 365 breakdown disrupted email services for businesses, hospitals and federal courts, while a separate FAA telecommunications failure triggered a nationwide ground stop.
 4 
 A customer uses Apple Pay on a credit card device. DenPhoto – stock.adobe.com 
 Advertisement
 There was no established connection between those incidents and Tuesday’s Apple service problems.
 The cause of Apple’s reported disruptions and the timetable for restoring service remained unclear.
